data.body: A content item is an article in the annotated-node model: every block pairs its reader-facing body with editorial annotations the reader never sees. The published page renders only the projection.

Body fields

  • tracking
  • slug (required)
  • title (required)
  • deck
  • description
  • author
  • image
  • taxonomy
  • seo
  • nodes (required)
  • chat
  • editorial
  • emotional_strategy
  • sources
  • claims
  • compliance
  • publication_context
  • lineage
  • scores

Patch operations

  • set_article_meta — Merge article meta fields (title/slug/author/taxonomy/seo/scores/…); nodes are edited only via node ops.
  • upsert_node
  • update_node
  • move_node
  • set_node_visibility
  • remove_node
  • set_tracking

This reference is generated from the live object_contract. If it disagrees with the contract, the manual is wrong and the drift guard fails the build of it.

Worked example

Why Everything in the CMS Is an Object was converted from misplaced tenant test content by typed metadata and node operations. Its public nodes explain architecture while private annotations remain outside reader HTML.

Lifecycle note

Slug and taxonomy must resolve, at least one public node must remain, and media references must follow the tenant artifact trust rules.
